### Decomposition {#sec-decomposition}

With the original parameters in @tbl-original-parameters, we can switch each source of disagreement on and off,
and see how the share of pupils that are eligible for a higher track changes.
To compare the tests on the same pupils, we let the whole national population take each test.
Similar to @eq-national-share, the national population is the combination of the test populations in @eq-common-factor,
weighted by the number of pupils $N_t$ that took each test:

$$
\theta_p \sim \sum_t w_t \mathcal{N}(\mu_t, \sigma^2_{\theta, t}), \quad w_t = \frac{N_t}{\sum_{t'} N_{t'}}.
$$ {#eq-national-population}

Since we assume the teacher and the test make their errors in measuring $\theta_p$ independently (see @sec-measurement-model),
we can use Equations [-@eq-teacher], [-@eq-test], and [-@eq-thresholds],
to compute the probabilities that the teacher gives the provisional advice $i$ and that the test $t$ gives the test result $j$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\PP(L_p = i \mid \theta_p) &=
\Phi\left(\frac{\lambda_{i+1} - \theta_p}{\sigma_L}\right) -
\Phi\left(\frac{\lambda_i - \theta_p}{\sigma_L}\right), \\
\PP_t(T_p = j \mid \theta_p) &=
\Phi\left(\frac{\tau_{j+1} - \alpha_t \theta_p - \beta_t}{\sigma_{T, t}}\right) -
\Phi\left(\frac{\tau_j - \alpha_t \theta_p - \beta_t}{\sigma_{T, t}}\right).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-category-probabilities}

The share of eligible pupils $\tilde{h}_t$, given the whole national population took the test $t$, is then given by:

$$
\tilde{h}_t = \sum_{i, j : G(i, j) > 0} \EE_\theta \left[ \PP(L_p = i \mid \theta_p) \PP_t(T_p = j \mid \theta_p) \right],
$$ {#eq-eligibility}

i.e., the model's counterpart of the standardized eligibility $h_t$ in @eq-standardized-eligibility.
We evaluate the expectation over the national population numerically, on a fine grid of $\theta$ values.
Switching an error off means setting its standard deviation to zero.
Then the teacher or the test reads the common factor exactly,
and the probability in @eq-category-probabilities is one for the category that contains the error and zero otherwise.

We attribute the eligibility to three sources:

- **teacher error** ($L$): the teacher's error $\sigma_L$ instead of zero,
- **test error** ($T$): the test's error $\sigma_{T, t}$ instead of zero, and
- **test menu** ($M$): the parameters $(\alpha_t, \beta_t, \sigma_{T, t})$ of the test $t$ instead of the parameters of the reference test.

Let $\tilde{h}(S)$ be the eligibility when the sources in the set $S \subseteq \{L, T, M\}$ are switched on, and the others are off.
When all sources are off, both the teacher and the reference test are perfect,
and the only remaining reason for eligibility is the mismatch between the two scales.
Therefore, $\tilde{h}(\emptyset)$ is the *category design* source of disagreement.

The contribution of a source depends on the order in which the sources are switched on, because the sources interact.
For example, how much eligibility the test error adds depends on where the test's thresholds lie relative to the teacher's thresholds,
which is what the test menu changes.
Therefore, we use the Shapley value [@shapley1953],
which averages the contribution of a source $k$ over all $3! = 6$ orders in which the sources can be switched on:

$$
\text{Sh}_k = \sum_{S \subseteq \{L, T, M\} \setminus \{k\}}
\frac{|S|! \, (2 - |S|)!}{3!}
\left[ \tilde{h}(S \cup \{k\}) - \tilde{h}(S) \right].
$$ {#eq-shapley}

The weight of a set $S$ is the share of the orders in which exactly the sources in $S$ are switched on before $k$.
Since the contributions along each order add up to the total change in eligibility, so do their averages:

$$
\tilde{h}_t = \tilde{h}(\emptyset) + \text{Sh}_L + \text{Sh}_T + \text{Sh}_M.
$$ {#eq-decomposition}

The test menu contribution $\text{Sh}_M$ is negative for the tests that are stricter than the reference test, and zero for the reference test itself.

```{r}
#| label: decomposition-values
#| include: false
pp <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", 100 * x)

decomposition_of <- function(year, test_name = reference_test) {
    filter(decomposition, test_year == year, test == test_name)
}

strictest_test <- function(year) {
    decomposition |>
        filter(test_year == year) |>
        slice_min(test_menu)
}

ref_2025 <- decomposition_of(2025)
ref_2026 <- decomposition_of(2026)
year_2026 <- filter(decomposition, test_year == 2026)
```

@fig-decomposition shows the decomposition per test, for the chosen year.
If the whole national population took the reference test in 2026,
`{r} pp(ref_2026$eligible)`% of pupils would be eligible for a higher track.
Category design accounts for `{r} pp(ref_2026$category_design)` percentage points,
teacher error for `{r} pp(ref_2026$teacher_error)`, and test error for `{r} pp(ref_2026$test_error)`.
In 2025, these were `{r} pp(ref_2025$category_design)`, `{r} pp(ref_2025$teacher_error)`, and `{r} pp(ref_2025$test_error)`
out of `{r} pp(ref_2025$eligible)`%.
Hence, `{r} sprintf("%.0f", 100 * ref_2026$category_design / ref_2026$eligible)`% of the eligibility would remain even if both the teacher and the test were perfect,
and the teacher error adds about `{r} round(ref_2026$teacher_error / ref_2026$test_error)` times as much eligibility as the test error.

Across the tests in 2026, the teacher error contributes between
`{r} pp(min(year_2026$teacher_error))`% and `{r} pp(max(year_2026$teacher_error))`%,
and the test error between
`{r} pp(min(year_2026$test_error))`% and `{r} pp(max(year_2026$test_error))`%.
The test menu contribution is largest for `{r} strictest_test(2026)$test`, which removes
`{r} pp(-strictest_test(2026)$test_menu)`% in 2026
(`{r} strictest_test(2025)$test`, `{r} pp(-strictest_test(2025)$test_menu)`% in 2025).
I.e., taking the strictest test instead of the reference test removes more eligibility than the teacher error adds for any test.

```{r}
#| label: fig-decomposition
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "Shapley decomposition of the share of pupils eligible for a higher track, if the whole national population took the test, per test (choose the year above the plot). Bars stack category design, teacher error, and test error; the hatched band is the eligibility that the test menu removes (since the reference test is the least strict); dots mark the total. Source: model fitted to CvTE [@cvte2025; @cvte2026], with Cito's resit share [@cito2026]."  # nolint: line_length_linter
decomposition_plot(decomposition)
```
